questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The multiplicative identity for rational numbers is
questions.explanation: Any rational number multiplied by 1 stays unchanged.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The sum of the first n odd natural numbers is always equal to
questions.answer: n²

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The relation between profit (P), cost price (C) and selling price (S) is
questions.answer: S = P + C
questions.explanation: Profit = S − C, so S = P + C.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The factorization of m² − 9 is
questions.explanation: m² − 3² is a difference of two squares.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The number of zeros in the square of 400 is
questions.explanation: 400² = 160000, which has 4 zeros.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Define quadrilateral.
questions.answer: A closed figure bounded by four line segments.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Write all possible outcomes when a fair coin is tossed once.
questions.answer: Head (H) and Tail (T).

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: In which year did the Government of India introduce GST?
questions.explanation: GST came into effect on 1 July 2017.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Name the proportion in which the product of two quantities is always a constant.
questions.answer: Inverse proportion

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Two quantities 'x' and 'y' are directly proportional. Write this statement in mathematical form.
questions.answer: x/y = k (a constant), i.e. x = ky

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Verify the commutative property of addition for the rational numbers 2/3 and 4/3.
questions.answer: 2/3 + 4/3 = 6/3 = 2 and 4/3 + 2/3 = 6/3 = 2. Both sums are equal, so addition is commutative.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: A spinning wheel has three green sectors, one blue sector and one red sector. What is the probability of getting a green sector?
questions.explanation: Favourable outcomes 3 out of 5 equally likely sectors.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The sale of fans on the first six days of a week is shown in a pictograph (one symbol = 2 fans). (a) On which day were the maximum number of fans sold? (b) How many fans were sold on Friday?
questions.answer: (a) Tuesday (b) 14 fans (7 symbols × 2)
questions.review: Symbol counts read from the PDF picture (Friday = 7 symbols). Confirm against the PDF; the picture is not stored.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Is 243 a perfect cube? Give reason.
questions.answer: No. 243 = 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 × 3, so the prime factor 3 occurs 5 times, which is not a multiple of 3.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: A person buys a T.V. for ₹40,000 and the GST rate is 28%. What is the GST amount?

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Find the product of (x − y²)(x² − y).
questions.answer: x³ − xy − x²y² + y³
questions.explanation: x·x² − x·y − y²·x² + y²·y.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Evaluate: (12⁴ × 9³ × 4) / (6³ × 8² × 27)
questions.explanation: Numerator = 2¹⁰·3¹⁰; denominator = 2⁹·3⁶; result = 2 × 3⁴ = 162.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The perimeter of a rectangular field is 154 m. If its length is 2 m more than its breadth, find the length and breadth of the field.
questions.answer: Breadth = 37.5 m, length = 39.5 m

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Find the smallest whole number by which 2028 should be multiplied to make it a perfect square. Also find the square root of the number so obtained.
questions.explanation: 2028 = 2² × 3 × 13², so the single factor 3 needs a partner.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The volume of a given mass of gas is inversely proportional to the pressure applied on it. If at a pressure of 100 Pa its volume is 8 litres, find its volume when the pressure is 200 Pa.
questions.answer: 4 litres
questions.explanation: P × V is constant: 100 × 8 = 200 × V, so V = 4.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Find the factors of 4ab − a² − 4b² + c².
questions.explanation: Group as c² − (a² − 4ab + 4b²) = c² − (a − 2b)².

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Find the values of x and y in the parallelogram ABCD, whose diagonals meet at O with AO = 5y + 1, OC = 6y − 1, BO = 3x − 1 and OD = 2(x + 1).
questions.explanation: Diagonals of a parallelogram bisect each other: 5y+1 = 6y−1 gives y = 2; 3x−1 = 2x+2 gives x = 3.
questions.review: Paper marks this 4. Labels read from the figure; confirm against the PDF.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: The length of a room is 12 ft, its breadth is 9 ft and the height of the wall is 8 ft. Find the cost of painting the inner walls at ₹50 per square foot.
questions.explanation: Area of four walls = 2(l + b)h = 2 × 21 × 8 = 336 sq ft; cost = 336 × 50.

questions.subject: Math
questions.text: Draw a graph for the table: apples 2, 4, 6, 8, 10 and cost (₹) 10, 20, 30, 40, 50, using suitable scales. From the graph answer: (a) Does the graph pass through the origin? (b) What is the cost of 5 apples? (c) How many apples can be bought for ₹45?
questions.answer: The points lie on a straight line through the origin. (a) Yes (b) ₹25 (c) 9 apples
questions.explanation: Cost = ₹5 per apple.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: The famous work of Hiuen Tsang is
questions.answer: Si-yu-ki
questions.explanation: Hiuen Tsang's travel account of India is Si-yu-ki.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Meaning and Importance of Political Science
questions.text: The father of political science is
questions.answer: Aristotle
questions.explanation: Aristotle is regarded as the father of political science.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: The Indian university that introduced Sociology for the first time is
questions.answer: Mumbai University
questions.explanation: Bombay (Mumbai) University began teaching Sociology in 1919.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Physical and intellectual work conducted for monetary benefit is
questions.answer: Economic activity
questions.explanation: Work done for money or income is an economic activity.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: The act that provides for the registration of partnership firms is
questions.answer: Indian Partnership Act – 1932
questions.explanation: The Indian Partnership Act of 1932 governs partnership firms and their registration.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Who presides over the Gram Sabha meetings?
questions.answer: The President (Adhyaksha) of the Gram Panchayat.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What is culture?
questions.answer: Culture is the way of life of a society: its customs, beliefs, language, arts and values passed from generation to generation.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Define social interaction.
questions.answer: Social interaction is the mutual action and response between two or more people.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: How old is the Earth?
questions.answer: About 4.6 billion years.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What is internal trade?
questions.answer: Buying and selling of goods and services within the borders of one country.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Ancient Indian Civilizations: Sindhu-Saraswati Civilization and Vedic Civilization
questions.text: Explain the significance of the Great Bath of Mohenjo-Daro.
questions.answer: The Great Bath was a large public water tank built of burnt bricks and made waterproof with bitumen. It shows the advanced engineering of the Indus people and was probably used for ritual bathing.
questions.explanation: This is the first half of an either/or question (the other is the Great Wall of China).

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Mention the historical significance of the Great Wall of China.
questions.answer: It was built to defend China from northern invaders, shows great engineering, and is a symbol of China and a World Heritage Site.
questions.explanation: This is the second half of an either/or question (the other is the Great Bath).

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Which are the four Noble Truths preached by Buddha?
questions.answer: 1) There is suffering in life. 2) Desire is the cause of suffering. 3) Suffering can be ended by ending desire. 4) The way to end it is the Eightfold Path.
questions.explanation: This is the first half of an either/or question (the other is Sanatana Dharma).

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: What are the specialties of Sanatana Dharma?
questions.answer: It is an ancient, universal way of life based on dharma, truth and non-violence, accepts many paths to the divine, and respects all beings and nature.
questions.explanation: This is the second half of an either/or question (the other is the four Noble Truths).

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: "A citizen performs several duties as a member of a country." Justify this statement.
questions.answer: A citizen pays taxes, obeys laws, respects the Constitution and national symbols, protects public property and defends the country when needed.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: List out the characteristics of an agricultural society.
questions.answer: People depend on farming, live in villages, have simple technology, follow seasons and festivals tied to crops, and have strong family and community ties.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: How are the location, direction and distance of a place determined?
questions.answer: Location by latitude and longitude, direction with a compass and the cardinal points, and distance using the map scale.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Explain the types of cooperative societies.
questions.answer: Common types are consumer, producer, credit, marketing, housing and farming cooperative societies.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: The Gupta period was a golden age of literature. Justify.
questions.answer: Kalidasa wrote Shakuntala, Meghaduta and Raghuvamsha; Vishakhadatta, Shudraka and Vishnu Sharma also wrote then, and Sanskrit flourished with royal support.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: The Cholas and Hoysalas of Dwarasamudra
questions.text: Explain the features of Chola village administration.
questions.answer: Villages ran through assemblies called Ur and Sabha. Members were chosen by lot (kudavolai) from eligible villagers, with committees for tanks, gardens, justice and temples.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Differentiate between weather and climate.
questions.answer: Weather is the day-to-day condition of the atmosphere at a place and changes quickly. Climate is the average weather of a place over about 30 years and changes very slowly.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: List out the adverse effects of water pollution.
questions.answer: Diseases such as cholera and typhoid, death of aquatic life, unsafe drinking water, lower crop quality and loss of biodiversity.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Explain the importance of labour.
questions.answer: Labour is a factor of production: it turns resources into goods and services, gives people income and drives economic growth.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Explain the salient features of the democratic system.
questions.answer: Rule by the people through elected representatives, free and fair periodic elections, equality before law, fundamental rights, rule of law and independent courts.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.text: Ocean tides benefit human life. Justify.
questions.answer: High tides let ships enter ports, tidal energy gives electricity, tides help fishing and clear harbours of silt, and spring tides help salt production.
questions.review: Paper marks this 4. Chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Social Science
questions.chapter: Bharathavarsha: Geographical Features and Prehistoric Period
questions.text: Draw an outline map of India and mark the following places: A) Talakadu B) Ajanta C) Kanchi D) Himalayan Range.
questions.answer: Outline map of India with the four places marked and labelled in their correct positions.
questions.review: Map question; chapter is a best guess.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: An inexhaustible resource among the following is
questions.answer: Solar light
questions.explanation: Sunlight will not run out; coal, petroleum and natural gas are limited.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Two individuals X and Y of equal weight stand on sand. X lies horizontally and Y stands vertically. Which statement is correct?
options: Pressure is independent of weight of the person.
questions.answer: Individual Y exerts more pressure.
questions.explanation: Same force on a smaller area gives more pressure.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Finest powder is sprinkled over the board while playing carrom because it
options: increases the efficiency of the game.
decreases the easy movement of carrom pawns
gives a good fragrance while playing
maintains the good condition of the carrom board
questions.answer: increases the efficiency of the game.
questions.explanation: The powder reduces friction so the pawns slide easily.
questions.review: Intended answer is 'reduces friction'; option A is the closest. Confirm.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter_guess: Conservation of Plants and Animals / Deforestation
questions.text: The main cause of desertification is
questions.answer: Destruction of forests
questions.explanation: Without tree cover, soil loses moisture and is eroded.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The light ray that strikes any surface is called
questions.answer: incident ray
questions.explanation: The ray that falls on a surface is the incident ray.

questions.subject: Science
questions.chapter: The Invisible Living World: Beyond Our Naked Eye
questions.text: Draw the diagram of Chlamydomonas.
questions.answer: A single oval cell with two flagella at the front, a cup-shaped chloroplast, a pyrenoid, a nucleus, an eyespot and a cell wall, all labelled.
questions.review: Drawing question; answer is guidance for the marker.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Mention the seasons for the cultivation of rabi and kharif crops.
questions.answer: Rabi crops: winter (October to March). Kharif crops: rainy season (June to October).

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Give an example that involves both muscular force and gravitational force.
questions.answer: Lifting a bucket of water from a well.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: The Malabar giant squirrel is an endangered species. Suggest one method to conserve it.
questions.answer: Protect its forest habitat by stopping deforestation and creating protected areas.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: How does a visually impaired person read?
questions.answer: By touch, using the Braille system of raised dots.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Mention the different techniques followed to store harvested grains.
questions.answer: Drying the grains in the sun, using neem leaves or chemicals against pests, and storing them in silos, granaries or gunny bags.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: List any four effects of force on objects.
questions.answer: A force can start or stop an object, change its speed, change its direction, or change its shape.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: How does reforestation help in the conservation of flora and fauna?
questions.answer: It restores habitats, brings back plants and animals, prevents soil erosion and keeps the water cycle balanced.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: In the given diagram, tester A has tap water and tester B has sea water. In which tester does the compass needle deflect more? Give reason.
questions.answer: Tester B (sea water). Sea water has more dissolved salts, so it conducts better, a larger current flows and the needle deflects more.
questions.review: Depends on a diagram; answer follows the labels in the PDF.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Earthquakes are considered as disasters. Justify this statement.
questions.answer: They strike without warning and destroy buildings, roads and bridges, cause loss of life and injury, and trigger fires and landslides.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Draw the diagram to show the structure of the human eye.
questions.answer: Diagram labelling the cornea, iris, pupil, lens, retina, optic nerve, ciliary muscles, vitreous humour and aqueous humour.
questions.review: Drawing question; answer is guidance for the marker.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Briefly explain any three methods of food preservation.
questions.answer: Heating or boiling (kills microbes), drying or dehydration (removes moisture), and refrigeration (slows microbial growth). Salting, sugaring, pickling and canning also work.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: (a) 'Friction is a kind of boon.' Explain. (b) Write two uses of lubricating (abrasive) oil.
questions.answer: (a) Friction lets us walk, grip objects, write, and brake vehicles. (b) A lubricating oil reduces friction and wear in machine parts and makes parts move smoothly.
questions.review: The paper says 'abrasive oil'; a lubricant is almost certainly meant. Confirm.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A plastic plate is struck with a steel spoon in a vacuum chamber. (a) Which material(s) vibrate? (b) Do you hear the sound? Justify.
questions.answer: (a) Both the plate and the spoon vibrate. (b) No, sound needs a medium such as air to travel, and a vacuum has none.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Draw a diagram showing the flow of electricity through water. Label (i) the carbon plate and (ii) the battery.
questions.answer: Circuit with a battery, a bulb or LED, and two carbon rods dipping in a beaker of water, with the carbon plates and battery labelled.
questions.review: Drawing question; answer is guidance for the marker.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: A teenager panics while watching a scary movie. (a) Name the hormone secreted to increase the heartbeat. (b) Name the gland responsible. (c) Is insulin produced in an emergency situation?
questions.answer: (a) Adrenaline. (b) The adrenal gland. (c) No, insulin is made by the pancreas and controls blood sugar.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Explain how petroleum is formed in nature.
questions.answer: Dead sea plants and animals sank to the sea floor and were covered by mud and sand. Over millions of years, heat, pressure and lack of air turned them into petroleum and natural gas, which were trapped between rock layers.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: Draw a diagram of the structure of the human male reproductive system. Label (i) the part responsible for sperm production and (ii) the sperm duct.
questions.answer: Diagram showing the testes (sperm production, label i), sperm duct (vas deferens, label ii), epididymis, urethra, penis and scrotum.

questions.subject: Science
questions.text: (a) Using a glass chimney, a candle, a wooden block and a glass plate, explain an activity to show that air is necessary for combustion. (b) Is air an ideal fuel? Justify.
questions.answer: (a) Place a lit candle on the table and cover it with the chimney resting on the wooden blocks so air enters from below; the candle burns. Cover the top with the glass plate and the flame goes out as the air is used up. (b) No. Air does not burn; it only supports combustion.
